title: Adaptive eval guardrail for canaries using per-customer golden prompt sets
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Ship an adaptive, low-noise evaluation guardrail that prevents canary progression when model quality degrades for a customer's production workload. This ticket covers: (1) per-customer golden prompt set storage and management, (2) an eval scoring pipeline that runs against shadow traffic and canary responses, (3) adaptive threshold computation based on baseline performance and traffic volume, and (4) automatic canary progression gating + rollback hooks integrated with the Console and rollout orchestration.

Scope and constraints:
- We will not attempt to replace human review for complex semantic regressions; the system should prioritize early blocking for high-severity regressions and surface candidates for human triage.
- Support per-route and per-customer golden sets; where a customer has no golden set, fallback to org-level defaults.
- Metrics include embedding-similarity (cosine), hallucination signals (tooling from R&D), and task-specific heuristics (e.g., instruction-following pass/fail).
- The pipeline must be resilient: compute scores asynchronously from production traffic using shadow copies, with options for synchronous gating on small canaries.

Why different from existing work: instead of a single global scorecard we will compute adaptive thresholds personalized to each customer's baseline and traffic profile, and fuse shadow-scored signals to reduce false positives before triggering auto-rollback.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Per-customer golden prompt set can be created/updated via Console and stored in the eval service.
2) Shadow scoring pipeline consumes live shadowed requests and writes per-prompt per-model scores to the eval DB.
3) Adaptive thresholding: for each (customer, route) determine a baseline distribution and compute an alert threshold that tightens with sample size but is robust to outliers.
4) Canary orchestration consults the eval guardrail: canary cannot progress beyond configured step if any critical metric exceeds threshold for N sequential windows.
5) Auto-rollback executes a safe rollback (no-op for Dedicated private customers without permission) and posts an incident summary to the rollout dashboard.
6) Console dashboard shows per-prompt deltas, rolling z-scores, and a single high-level pass/fail decision for each canary.
activity_log: 2026-02-28: Ticket created during Rollouts guild sync — scoped per-customer golden dataset requirement.
2026-03-02: Architecture review with Runtime and Console teams. Decided to store golden sets in eval-service S3 bucket with metadata in eval-postgres.
2026-03-04: Prototype scoring job implemented for embedding similarity and persisted to eval-timeseries. Initial tests on 5 customers show stable baselines.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM and Design — decided on visualizations and required fields for golden prompt editors in Console.
2026-03-10: Implemented adaptive threshold algorithm (percentile + shrinkage) and smoke-tested on synthetic regressions. Reduced false-positive rate vs fixed-threshold by ~40% in bench tests.
2026-03-12: Begin wiring guardrail checks into rollout controller; first end-to-end canary blocked as expected during staged test (internal-only).
notes: Decision: use a hybrid scoring signal (embedding cosine + binary heuristics) to balance sensitivity and explainability.

Trade-off: tighter per-customer thresholds reduce risk of noisy rollbacks but increase the chance of false negatives for low-traffic customers; mitigation = require sustained regression windows before rollback and route-level manual overrides.
Operational hook: when a canary is blocked, create a pre-filled incident with representative failing prompts and model responses for SRE/PM review.
Follow-up: add a calibration job (weekly) that re-computes baselines after large model-version upgrades and flags customers whose golden sets are stale.
